What this app holds

Nothing here is hidden until later. This page says in plain words where every journey in the app leads, so that no one is led for weeks toward a destination they were not told about.

What we hold

  1. God is one. There is no god but Him, and every messenger was sent with that one sentence (21:25).
  2. The religion is one. Noah, Abraham, Moses, Jesus and Muhammad were given the same religion to establish and were told not to divide in it (42:13). Laws and ways differ by nation; the religion does not (5:48).
  3. People were one community and people divided it. The division came after knowledge, through rivalry (42:14, 10:19). The verses that say so are addressed to every party, and this app reads them first as a word to its own readers.
  4. The Quran is the true, preserved book. Every answer rests on it. Beside it we show passages from earlier scriptures that agree with it, each with its source, so that you can see the one message for yourself.
  5. A person calls on God directly. Each person's prayer reaches God directly (2:186, 40:60). This does not mean nobody may pray for you; the Quran commends praying for others.
  6. Deeds are weighed, and mercy stays in the picture. The scale is just and no good deed is lost, down to an atom's weight (21:47, 99:7-8). The same book keeps the door of mercy open (39:53). Faith and deed go together (18:110).
  7. The Prophet's family and his noble companions are loved and honoured. The app speaks of his family in the words every Muslim already uses in prayer. It does not enter questions of historical dispute and issues no ruling on them.

What we do not do

  • We do not issue religious rulings. The app states what a verse says and then asks.
  • We do not call any person, group or practice names. Words that judge people are kept out of the app's own voice; the verses are shown as they are.
  • We do not name any community as the subject of a fault. Where a verse speaks of parties content with what they hold, it is read of the reader's own party first.
  • We do not teach that all religions are the same or should be merged. We show what the books share, and the Quran remains the criterion.
  • We do not change the message for the reader. Only the entry point, the depth and the form of reasoning change.

What you will meet, and in what order

First, your own question, answered with the Quran's reasoning. Then, if you wish, the seven places of the road: one nation, one order, one religion, how people divided, why, each party content, and the way back. Beyond the road, three more: the path, stewardship on earth, and the scale. Nothing on this page is withheld from a reader who asks; the order decides only what is offered first.

Where the texts come from

The Quran text is the Tanzil Uthmani text, unchanged. Every other passage is shown with its book and verse number, and its edition is named on the sources page. See the sources.
